interpretation: Longer consecutive pre-loss Thalassia history at the same meter mark predicts one-year re-recording after a one-year loss even after stable transect identity, loss-year vegetation state, source-year mixed-species state, and loss year are represented. This supports a local persistence-legacy signal but does not distinguish residual rhizomes/clonal structure from persistent microsite quality or repeated detectability.
next_hypothesis: Test the legacy effect specifically among loss-year seagrass-bare meter marks. Persistence of the effect without above-ground seagrass continuity would strengthen a subterranean/local-legacy interpretation while still not proving rhizome causality.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc temporal ecology on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
The coefficient is on a standardized within-node centered run-length predictor; do not interpret 0.451 as a per-year log-odds effect.
Do not call this direct evidence of clonal memory or residual rhizomes without below-ground measurements.
Stable node identity and community-continuity controls reduce but do not eliminate confounding by persistent microsite habitat quality or detectability.
Re-recording is an observation-state return, not genet-level recolonization.
